questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: living and working abroad in a smaller city with great nature surroundings

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1) language: As the language barrier plays a huge role when doing clinical rotations/ interacting with patients, I was only looking for exchange to Scandinavian, English- or German-speaking countries. 
2) clinical rotations: I wanted to see as many different departments as possible during my exchange 
3) personal experience: I wanted to try living in a smaller city surrounded by mountains

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Not very easy. 
I found it very confusing to be communicating with many different people: Monika Schlager from International Office, D. Mulser from KPJ-Anmeldung (responsible for all clinical stays), and the secretaries from the different departments. 
I didn't have enough insight in their organisation and therefore didn't know who to ask/ who would be responsible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Little assistance. 
I knew which departments I had been assigned to during the three months. 
I also knew where and when to show up the first day, but the whole procedure with picking up the staff card, clothes, log-in etc. was very confusing and poorly planned/communicated. 
I didn't recieve any up-front information about what to expect of the first day of the clinical stay or in general the whole clincal stay. No information about working hours, holidays, no general information about the departments I would be placed at, a map of the hospital etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
The arrival and first days of my clinical stay were a disaster and made me reconsider my choice. 
This is not a critique of personal matter, as M. Schlager and especially D. Mulser from KPJ-Anmeldung were very helpful, I just would have wished for a better organised introduction. A student buddy would also have made a great difference: someone to show you around on campus, where to get the clothes, how the canteen works etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
it was difficult finding housing. 
I didn't want to live in any of the large student dorms, so I had to get creative. Got lucky with one holiday house that I was able to rent for the whole period. 
other recommendations: facebook "wohnungsbörse innsbruck"

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: take into account that Innsbruck is surrounded by mountains and if you live on the hillside, there might not be public transportation all the way and you might not be able to bike down-/uphill during winter. Snow is likely from Nov-March

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I would have wished for a better overview of all the steps needed. As written above, I found it very confusing to be communicating with a lot of different people.  
Other than that, I don't remember the registration process as complicated, also because my course "clinical stay in foreign country" was relatively fixed

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: communication with M. Schlager from International office and Anne Fledelius from the Int. office from my home university, UCPH

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: though there were only few options available for my clinical rotations, I was satisfied with the three departments that I got: gynecology, infectious medicine, orthopedic surgery

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: it might seem a lot of work, but get it done as fast as possible so you can start to get excited for your exchange!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: clinical stay with different levels of supervision from the department's physicians

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
the clinical stays at my host institution (Innsbruck) seemed more disorganised and the organisation and teaching heavily depends on each department, far more than I was used to from home. 
There are no teaching classes apart from "fortbildungen"/"forlæsninger", which is not discussion-based. There was very little time or interest from the doctors, to discuss cases or treatments etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: clinical stay in foreign country, 20 ECTS

questions.answer: food and rent was more expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: for future exchange students: be sure to check for sport courses at USI well in advance, as they get sold out very fast

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: due to corona, I didn't have the impression of a lot of activities going on

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- sport courses at USI
- Whatsapp/Telegram interest groups (table tennis, skiing, hiking, beachvolley, chess, spike ball etc..)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
explore the nature around Innsbruck!
Weekend trip to Munich, Salzburg, Northern Italy

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was not a very big adjustment for me as I already knew the German culture. 
I still got surprised by how relatively conservative Austria still is

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: as written above: engage in different sports, maybe even create your own group and share your interests

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
how everyone appreciates being out in the nature in their free time, 
great food and beautiful architecture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) arrive two or three weeks prior to your clinical exchange, so you can settle down and meet people, maybe even make connections with someone who can show you around on the campus 
2) don't plan too much beforehand on what you want to see or do while you're on exchange 
3) start looking for housing minimum 2 months before and prioritize finding a place that you can rent for the whole period

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: completing the exchange, although I thought about quitting several times in the beginning

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: social challenges: not feeling welcome at a deparment, feeling "stuck" because you are assigned at a specific department and going somewhere else is not impossible but complicated, feeling left alone and not seen as a ressource (I was the only student in the department during the first month).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
